promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 6 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: You hit 20 miles and it felt good, but the week ran 40 percent over plan after a big jump the week before, so next week pulls back on purpose to let the gains stick.

answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer: Short answer: no, not for another week. You just did two jumps back to back (37 to 53 miles, and 14 to 20 on the long run), and the body banks that work on the week after, not the week of. If we stack another "felt fine so I added more" week on top, the knee twinge from a few weeks ago or the tight calves become the story again. We are 6 weeks out, which is exactly the moment to consolidate, sharpen marathon pace, and arrive at the start line healthy. Hold next week to the plan as written, then I will build the long run back toward 20 to 22 with marathon-pace work inside it over the following two weeks.

new.analysis:
The reviewed week delivered the fitness we wanted, but through a route I would not have chosen. The prescribed load was ~38 miles with one threshold and a 15-mile long run; you ran ~53 miles, added a Monday run, lengthened every easy day, took a 4th threshold rep, and pushed the long run to 20. Nothing broke, which is a credit to how you are absorbing training, but the overload flag is real.

The signals I like: easy heart rate held at 139 bpm at 9:50/mi pace, drift on easy days stayed small, and the long run averaged 10:02/mi at 149 bpm with only a 7 bpm drift over 20 miles. That is a strong aerobic signature for a sub-3:45 build. The signals I am cautious about: 88 percent of the long run sat in zone 3, calves were tight that night, and the week's effort score was almost twice your recent average.

So next week is a deliberate consolidation at about 40 miles. The quality session shifts to marathon pace (8:35/mi for your 3:45 goal), because that is the specific work that matters most now. The long run comes down to 15 easy to let the 20-miler settle. If this week lands clean, the week of Sep 21 goes long again with marathon-pace segments inside it, and that becomes your peak long run before we taper.

One ask: run the plan as written this time, including the shorter days. The discipline to hold back when you feel good is the same muscle you will need at mile 18 on race day.
